title: Direct summands of perfect complexes are perfect
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let K and L be objects of the derived category D(\mathcal{O}_X) [def-pc-derived-category]. If K is isomorphic to a direct sum L \oplus M for some object M and K is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex], then L is perfect (and likewise M is perfect).

proof.text: By [lem-pc-perfect-pseudo-coherent-locally-finite-tor], the perfect object K is pseudo-coherent and, on a neighbourhood of every point, has Tor amplitude in some interval [a,b].
The direct-summand decomposition and [lem-pc-pseudo-coherent-summand] imply that L (and similarly M) is pseudo-coherent.

source.place: Tag 08CE (pseudo-coherent complexes are closed under direct summands)

proof.text: On each neighbourhood from Step 1, the Tor-amplitude bound for K passes to the direct summand L (and M) by the additivity and direct-summand statement of Tag 08CK: tensoring with any module gives a direct-sum decomposition, so vanishing outside [a,b] is inherited by each summand.

source.place: Tag 08CK (finite Tor dimension is preserved by direct summands)

proof.text: On each such neighbourhood, L is pseudo-coherent and has finite Tor dimension, so [lem-pc-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect] makes L perfect there. Perfectness is local by [def-pc-perfect-complex], hence L is perfect on X; the same argument gives the conclusion for M.
